title: Getting started
summary: Install AIFENCE, mint a key, and run an artifact through the complete Quality → Guard → Bus fence.
text:
Install AIFENCE targets Python 3.12+. Create an isolated environment and install the repository in editable mode. bash python m venv .venv . .venv/bin/activate Windows: .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 pip install e ". dev " Optional extras include postgres , s3 , mcp , otel , quality full JSON Schema , redis , kafka , rabbitmq , and bench . Run bash aifence api The composed application serves on 0.0.0.0:8080 . In development it can create the schema automatically; in production use migrations. bash curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/health/ready json { "ready": true, "subsystems": "aifence.quality","aifence.guard","aifence.bus" , "region role": "active", "accepts writes": true } Create a tenant and API key Every authenticated surface uses guard issued keys. Bootstrap the first tenant and administrative key: bash python c " from aifence.app import create app from aifence.core.config import CoreSettings app = create app CoreSettings with app.state.session factory as s: t, k, secret = app.state.guard app.state.service.create tenant and key s, tenant name='Example Org', key name='bootstrap', scopes= ' ' print secret " The secret is printed once. Store it in a secret manager immediately. Run an artifact through the fence bash curl X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/fence/submit \ H "Authorization: Bearer $AIFENCE API KEY" \ H "Content Type: application/json" \ d '{ "artifact": " Q3 Report

Revenue grew 12% to $4.2M across all regions.", "content type": "text/markdown", "receiver": "analytics agent", "action": { "operation": "read" } }' A successful run returns final outcome: "handed off" and a durable message id the receiver can claim from the bus. Watch it block Placeholders fail the quality gate before enforcement runs: bash d '{"artifact": " Draft

TODO: write this.", "content type": "text/markdown"}' → blocked by quality A destructive, high risk action can pass quality but be stopped by Guard: bash d '{"artifact": "…", "action": {"operation": "delete", "destructive": true}, "risk score": 80}' → blocked by guard Next steps Fence flow fence flow.html — outcomes and the receipt format. Configuration configuration.html — the environment surface and fail closed settings. SDKs sdk.html — Python, TypeScript and Go clients with framework hooks. Deployment deployment.html — migrations, Helm and multi region topology.

title: Architecture
summary: How Quality, Guard, and Bus compose into one FastAPI control plane with one identity, database, audit chain, and telemetry pipeline.
text: AIFENCE is one FastAPI application built by one factory. It owns the shared foundation and then invites each installed subsystem to mount itself. text ┌───────────────── aifence.app.create app ──────────────────┐ │ middleware · error envelope · health · metrics · OpenAPI │ │ lifespan bridged · circuit breakers · identity │ └──────┬──────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────┘ │ register │ register │ register ┌──────▼─────┐ ┌──────▼──────┐ ┌──────▼──────┐ │ quality │────▶│ guard │────▶│ bus │ │ gate │ │ enforcement │ │ transport │ └────────────┘ └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘ └──────────────── aifence.core ───────────────┘ config · db one Base/engine · errors · middleware metrics · telemetry · env helpers Why a shared core rather than a single monolith The tiers share FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Alembic, pydantic, cryptography and Prometheus, but their domain configuration and models are distinct. aifence.core owns only the cross cutting infrastructure every tier uses, while each subsystem keeps its own settings, models and routers. The composition seam aifence.subsystems defines a register app, ctx protocol and discovers installed subsystems in flow order quality → guard → bus . create app never imports a subsystem directly. subsystems can be added or replaced without changing the factory; the application runs with any subset installed; each subsystem mounts its own router and wires workers into the shared lifespan; SubsystemContext hands each subsystem the shared settings, engine and session factory. Mounted sub applications Guard and Bus are mounted as FastAPI sub applications at /guard and /bus . They keep their proven internals and router level authentication while sharing the core engine, declarative Base , and metrics registry. Lifespans are bridged Starlette does not run a mounted application's lifespan. create app enters every mounted lifespan through an AsyncExitStack , so HTTP clients, workers and storage clients start and stop as one unit. OpenAPI is combined Sub app paths would otherwise live only under their mounted OpenAPI documents. The factory folds them into the root document, rebasing paths and namespacing component schemas to avoid collisions. Native routers Quality, the Fence flow and the operator console are composed directly onto the root application and are explicitly bound to the same identity model. One database, one migration history Every subsystem declares its models against aifence.core.db.Base , so one Alembic history builds the entire schema and one connection pool serves every tier. A migration/model drift test prevents undeclared schema changes. Data flow 1. Quality scores the artifact and emits a quality decision. 2. Guard compiles baseline + tenant policy into an enforcement plan and exact action capability. 3. Bus durably persists the vetted payload as a claimable handoff, then optionally fans out to a broker. Every step shares the request id, audit chain and telemetry established by the core.

title: Fence flow
summary: The three tiers as one governed pipeline, with short-circuiting, resilience budgets, and one truthful receipt.
text: The fence flow is what makes AIFENCE one system rather than three services sharing a host. A single authenticated request runs through all three tiers in process and returns one receipt describing what each tier decided. text POST /v1/fence/submit │ ├── quality gate ──── fails ──▶ blocked by quality guard never runs │ │ passes ├── guard enforcement ─ denies ─▶ blocked by guard bus never runs │ │ allows └── durable handoff ─── degraded ─▶ authorized not delivered │ delivered └──────────────────────▶ handed off Outcomes final outcome allowed Meaning handed off true Passed every tier; a claimable message was persisted. blocked by quality false The artifact failed the quality gate. blocked by guard false Policy denied or required approval. authorized not delivered true Permitted, but transport was degraded. authorized not delivered exists so the receipt never claims a handoff that did not happen. The receipt json { "request id": "req …", "tenant id": "ten …", "allowed": true, "final outcome": "handed off", "degraded tiers": , "stages": { "quality": { "passed": true, "score": 100 }, "guard": { "outcome": "allow", "matched rule": "baseline:read only low risk" }, "bus": { "delivered": true, "message id": "M…", "content ref": "aifence:sha256:…" } } } Resilience Every tier is fail closed by default: a tier that cannot answer within its latency budget causes 503 tier unavailable . Repeated failures trip a circuit breaker and short circuit the tier for a recovery window. quality and bus may be configured advisory. Guard cannot — naming it as fail open is rejected at startup. Grounding a submission Supplying sources enables the quality tier's grounding check for the whole flow, so fabricated figures are stopped before enforcement. Relationship to the Guard API Endpoint Use when POST /guard/v1/decisions You want an enforcement decision only. POST /v1/fence/submit You want the full pipeline and a durable handoff.

title: Quality tier
summary: Scores AI-generated artifacts against production quality controls before sensitive enforcement or transport runs.
text: The Quality tier is the first gate in the fence flow. It scores an AI generated artifact and decides whether it is fit to proceed. A failing artifact is stopped before Guard evaluates the action. Architecture text quality/source/control registry.csv ~1,000 canonical controls │ ▼ aifence.quality.controls loader, capability lookup │ ▼ aifence.quality.gate the in process gate The canonical quality control pack lives under the repository's top level quality/ directory. The Python package aifence.quality is a bridge that reads the control registry and runs a fast deterministic gate in process. Checks Check Weight Mandatory What it catches : completeness 40 yes An empty artifact. anti template 25 yes Unresolved TODO , TBD , PLACEHOLDER , Lorem ipsum . answerability 15 no Too little substance to be useful. link integrity 10 no Empty or placeholder links in markup. structure 10 no Missing headings or landmarks in markup. json validity 35 yes JSON artifacts that do not parse. schema conformance 25 yes Output violating a supplied JSON Schema. grounding 20 conditional Numeric claims absent from supplied sources. Outcomes accept — score meets the threshold and no mandatory check failed. revise — no mandatory failure, but the score is below min score . reject — a mandatory check failed. Score is irrelevant. This is why an artifact can score well and still be rejected: a single unresolved placeholder is disqualifying. Schema conformance With the quality extra installed, full JSON Schema validation applies. Without it, the gate falls back to a required property and type subset so a missing contract field is still caught rather than silently passing. Grounding Given sources , the gate reports numeric claims in the artifact that appear nowhere in the source material. One unsourced figure is a warning; a cluster of more than two fails the gate outright. json // sources say 4.2M / 12% / 1500 accounts "Revenue reached 9.9 million, up 87 percent, across 4200 accounts…" // → grounding: 4 numeric claim s absent from sources → reject API Endpoint Purpose GET /v1/quality/registry Summary of the loaded control registry. GET /v1/quality/controls List controls, filterable by priority. POST /v1/quality/evaluate Run the gate over an artifact.

title: Guard tier
summary: The enforcement plane — decides and enforces what an agent is permitted to do.
text: The Guard tier sits outside the agent process and evaluates every sensitive action before it reaches a provider, tool, data source, artifact store, or another agent. Required controls must compile into an executable enforcement plan or the operation fails closed. Decision pipeline text DecisionRequest │ ├─▶ detectors ──────▶ findings category, severity, confidence │ │ ├─▶ content classifier ──┤ observed data classes │ ▼ ├─▶ risk scoring ─────▶ risk 0–100 │ │ └─▶ policy engine ───────┴─▶ outcome + constraints │ ▼ enforcement plan → capability token Outcomes Outcome Meaning allow Proceed unchanged. allow with limits Proceed under constraints. redact or transform Proceed only after transformation. require approval Hold for a human decision. deny Refuse. quarantine and terminate Refuse, isolate the artifact, and end the run. Detectors Stable finding categories include prompt injection, data exfiltration, secret exposure, undeclared sensitive content, control evasion, instruction drift, material misrepresentation, fabricated completion, scope violations, disallowed tools, dangerous commands, and excessive delegation depth. Capability tokens An allowed decision does not itself perform the action. Guard issues an exact action capability token bound to the tool, operation, resource and arguments, with a TTL and maximum use count. A token obtained for one action cannot be replayed against another. Identity and access Tenants isolate data with PostgreSQL row level security. API keys are scoped and can be bound to an immutable agent manifest, workload, instance and principal. Workload identity can be provided through trusted SPIFFE assertions from a mutually authenticated proxy. Evidence Every decision produces a signed receipt and events are written to a hash chained audit log with periodic checkpoints. Checkpoints can be anchored to independently administered external destinations. Worker roles Guard separates control plane , dispatcher , lifecycle , anchor , migration , and maintenance runtime roles so durable work can scale independently. Production posture Production validation refuses to start without the configured hardening requirements: PostgreSQL/TLS, mTLS, non exportable signing, external KMS, durable evidence storage, independent audit anchoring, controlled egress, and workload identity.

title: Bus tier
summary: The semantic communication runtime — durable handoffs, content-addressed references, learned patterns, and minimum-sufficient state.
text: The Bus tier is a vendor neutral semantic communication runtime. It carries the minimum state a downstream agent needs rather than resending whole conversations: content addressed references, immutable deltas, learned compositional patterns, provenance, and a model of what the receiver already knows. Durable delivery text handoff ──▶ pending ──▶ claimed ──▶ acknowledged │ └─▶ lease expiry ──▶ claimable again A handoff is committed to the database before it is considered delivered. Receiver knowledge advances only after acknowledgement, so a claimed but unacked message is redelivered rather than lost. Semantic compression The bus compresses meaning rather than bytes. Negation, amounts, identities, authorization, deadlines, environment markers, instructions and constraints take the strict preservation path. Unknown or ambiguous meaning remains literal or referenced. Learned patterns Recurring semantic structures move through candidate, shadow validation and counterfactual evaluation before becoming active. Promotion accounts for frequency, savings, stability, ambiguity, source trust/diversity, holdout evidence and receiver specific fidelity. Content addressed references Stored content uses SHA 256 identity. Authorization and lifetime are separate grants, so identical bytes deduplicate without sharing authorization. Grants support workspace/owner scope, agent ACLs, field paths, memory tier, TTL, provenance and optional AES GCM encryption at rest. Broker transports Backend Mechanism Extra none No fan out default — memory In process, for tests — redis Redis Stream XADD redis kafka Topic keyed by receiver kafka rabbitmq Durable topic exchange rabbitmq Publication follows the durable commit, and events carry identity/routing metadata rather than semantic content. A broker outage is reported in the receipt instead of being converted into a false success. Protocol and conformance The bus reads and writes sage/0.2 , wire version 2. Protocol identity is canonical MessagePack plus SHA 256; JSON is the readable representation. A language neutral conformance kit of 13 normative vectors 6 valid, 7 invalid is consumed independently by Python, JavaScript and Go implementations.

title: Security model
summary: Shared identity, content classification, evidence, controlled egress, and an intentionally fail-closed posture.
text: One identity model Every authenticated AIFENCE surface uses the same API keys Guard issues. The fence flow, quality endpoints and operator console are explicitly bound to that provider rather than receiving a weaker credential path. Surface Authentication /health/live , /health/ready , /metrics Public where configured for probes/scrapers. /v1/fence/submit API key with decisions:write . /v1/quality/ API key. /v1/console/ API key with decisions:read . /guard/ Guard router level authentication. Scopes Keys carry explicit scopes such as decisions:read , decisions:write , approvals:write , capabilities:issue , audit:anchor , policies:activate , memory:quarantine , and tenants:lifecycle . Content classification Data classes can be declared by the caller, but enforcement does not trust declaration alone. AIFENCE inspects payloads and reports observed sensitive classes into the same exfiltration and secret exposure rules. Class Signal Precision measure financial Card numbers, IBANs Card numbers must pass a Luhn check. government id National IDs Structurally invalid ranges excluded. credential AWS/GitHub/Slack keys, JWTs Generic secrets require assignment context. secret Private key blocks Explicit PEM header. health Clinical terminology Reported signal. personal data Email, phone Informational class. Matched sensitive values are never returned — the classifier reports class names and counts only. Fail closed posture A tier that cannot answer produces 503 unless an allowed advisory tier is configured to fail open. Guard can never be configured to fail open. Unknown policy constraints fail closed rather than being ignored. A standby region refuses durable worker roles at startup. An unknown bus backend fails at startup instead of silently disabling fan out. Production validation refuses to start until hardening requirements are met. Evidence Decisions produce signed receipts. Events are written to a hash chained audit log with periodic checkpoints that can be anchored to independently administered destinations. Network controls Outbound calls are confined: HTTPS only destinations, canonical path confinement, DNS revalidation with connection time IP pinning, preserved TLS SNI and Host, no redirect following, controlled egress, and bounded response sizes.

title: Configuration
summary: The shared AIFENCE_ environment surface, resilience budgets, multi-region settings, policy profiles, and subsystem ownership.
text: Configuration is read from the environment and optionally .env . Every current variable uses the AIFENCE prefix. Invalid production configuration is rejected at startup and validation reports every unmet requirement at once. Core Variable Default Purpose AIFENCE ENVIRONMENT development development / test / staging / production . AIFENCE RUNTIME ROLE control plane Runtime role. AIFENCE LOG LEVEL INFO Root log level. AIFENCE BIND HOST 0.0.0.0 Bind host. AIFENCE BIND PORT 8080 Bind port. AIFENCE PUBLIC BASE URL http://localhost:8080 Advertised OpenAPI base URL. AIFENCE DOCS ENABLED true Expose docs/OpenAPI. AIFENCE MAX REQUEST BYTES 2097152 Global request body ceiling. Persistence Variable Default Purpose AIFENCE DATABASE URL sqlite+pysqlite:///./aifence.db SQLAlchemy URL. AIFENCE DB POOL SIZE 20 Pool size non SQLite . AIFENCE DB MAX OVERFLOW 20 Pool overflow. AIFENCE AUTO CREATE SCHEMA true Dev schema creation; use Alembic in production. Fence flow resilience Variable Default Purpose AIFENCE FLOW QUALITY TIMEOUT SECONDS 5.0 Quality latency budget. AIFENCE FLOW GUARD TIMEOUT SECONDS 5.0 Guard latency budget. AIFENCE FLOW BUS TIMEOUT SECONDS 10.0 Bus latency budget. AIFENCE FLOW FAILURE THRESHOLD 5 Failures before breaker trip. AIFENCE FLOW RECOVERY SECONDS 30.0 Recovery probe window. AIFENCE FLOW FAIL OPEN TIERS empty Advisory tiers permitted to fail open. Only Quality and Bus. Guard cannot be made fail open. Naming it is rejected at startup. Multi region and transport Variable Default Purpose AIFENCE REGION empty Region identifier. AIFENCE REGION ROLE active active owns writes/workers; standby serves reads. AIFENCE BUS TRANSPORT none none , memory , redis , kafka , rabbitmq . AIFENCE BUS TRANSPORT URL empty Broker URL. AIFENCE BUS TRANSPORT TOPIC aifence.handoffs Stream/topic/exchange name. Policy profiles AIFENCE GUARD POLICY FILE selects the policy document. Two measured profiles ship: strict and balanced . Balanced is designed to reduce approval friction while preserving the evaluated detection behavior when behavioral analysis is enabled. Secrets For secret backed variables, <NAME FILE can point to a mounted secret file. This lets containers and Helm consume secrets without placing them in pod specs.

title: Deployment
summary: Migrations, containers, Helm, production hardening, multi-region active/standby topology, and broker transports.
text: Database migrations Production should run with AIFENCE AUTO CREATE SCHEMA=false ; Alembic is the only thing that creates tables. bash alembic upgrade head A test asserts migrations produce the declared models and the history has one head, preventing silent schema drift. Container bash docker compose up build PostgreSQL + the control plane The image runs as a non root user and serves aifence api on port 8080. Helm The chart lives under deploy/helm/aifence and deploys the control plane plus dispatcher, lifecycle and audit anchor worker roles, migration job, network policy, HPA, PDB and ingress. bash helm upgrade install aifence deploy/helm/aifence f my values.yaml Production validation Production refuses to start without the configured hardening requirements, including verified TLS for PostgreSQL, mTLS, external KMS/non exportable signing, durable evidence storage, independent audit anchoring, controlled egress and workload identity. Multi region topology Exactly one region is active : it owns the writable database and durable workers. Other regions are standby : they can serve the control plane from replicas and remain warm for promotion. yaml active region: { name: eu west 1, role: active } standby region: { name: us east 1, role: standby } Three independent guardrails prevent a standby from behaving like the active region: 1. Startup validation refuses standby + durable worker role. 2. The Helm chart does not render durable workers/migration outside the active region. 3. Readiness publishes accepts writes , so a global load balancer sends writes only to active. Bus transports bash AIFENCE BUS TRANSPORT=redis AIFENCE BUS TRANSPORT URL=redis://redis:6379/0 AIFENCE BUS TRANSPORT TOPIC=aifence.handoffs Publication happens after the durable commit and carries routing identity rather than semantic content. Health and observability Path Purpose /health/live Liveness probe. /health/ready Readiness; reports region and accepts writes . /metrics Prometheus scrape target. Set AIFENCE OTEL EXPORTER OTLP ENDPOINT to enable OpenTelemetry tracing.

title: Operations
summary: Run the fence with operator status, health probes, Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry traces, and explicit degradation signals.
text: Operator console GET /v1/console/ renders an operator dashboard; GET /v1/console/status returns the same data as JSON. Both require decisions:read . The console shows: durable handoff counts by status; approvals pending for the caller's tenant; per tier circuit breaker state; composed subsystem status; quality control registry size; configured Bus transport. Health probes Path Use /health/live Liveness — is the process up? /health/ready Readiness, region and accepts writes . accepts writes is the critical global load balancer signal in an active/standby deployment. Metrics Prometheus metrics include shared HTTP counters/latency plus guard decision outcomes, capability/approval lifecycle, execution transitions, outbox backlog, dispatch/dependency latency, and audit anchor events. Tracing Setting AIFENCE OTEL EXPORTER OTLP ENDPOINT enables OpenTelemetry tracing for the application and SQLAlchemy. Health and metrics paths are excluded. Content payloads are not placed into span attributes. Reading a degraded run degraded tiers in the fence receipt names any tier that failed open. final outcome: "authorized not delivered" means authorization succeeded but transport did not persist a handoff. 503 tier unavailable means a fail closed tier could not answer. Verification bash make verify ruff + mypy strict + pytest make test

title: SDKs
summary: Python, TypeScript and Go clients, plus agent-framework enforcement hooks.
text: Maintained clients live under sdks/ . Language Path Package identifier Python sdks/python agentdance client TypeScript sdks/typescript @agentdance/client Go sdks/go agentdance Package identifiers are held stable so existing integrations keep compiling. Base URL: point at the Guard mount Guard is mounted at /guard and clients append /v1/... to the base URL: text https://aifence.example.com/guard → https://…/guard/v1/decisions HTTPS is required by every client. python from agentdance client import AgentDanceClient client = AgentDanceClient "https://aifence.example.com/guard", api key Framework integrations The Python SDK includes framework neutral hooks for OpenAI Agents, LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen and Semantic Kernel. Each wrapper submits a tool call for a decision before it executes; a denied decision raises rather than returning control to the tool. Two entry points Endpoint Use when POST /guard/v1/decisions Enforcement decision only. POST /v1/fence/submit Full Quality → Guard → Bus pipeline. Client behavior All clients use explicit timeouts, capped retries with Retry After awareness, no redirect following, maximum response size and AIFENCE's structured error envelope code , message , details , request id .

title: API reference
summary: The composed OpenAPI 3.1 surface: fence flow, Quality, Guard, Bus and operator endpoints.
text: The authoritative contract is the composed application's /openapi.json when documentation is enabled. The documented snapshot contains 165 endpoints . Fence flow Method Path Purpose POST /v1/fence/submit Run an artifact through Quality → Guard → Bus. Quality Method Path Purpose GET /v1/quality/controls List quality controls. POST /v1/quality/evaluate Run the quality gate. GET /v1/quality/registry Quality control registry summary. Console Method Path Purpose GET /v1/console/status Operational status across every fence tier. Guard resource groups Guard exposes endpoints beneath /guard/v1/ for agents, API keys, approvals, artifacts, audit anchors/checkpoints, budgets, capabilities, decisions, delegations, dispatch, events, executions, incidents, memory, operator posture, policies, protocols, providers, tenant lifecycle, tools, traces, workload identities and more. High value Guard endpoints Method Path Purpose POST /guard/v1/decisions Render an enforcement decision. POST /guard/v1/capabilities Issue exact action capability. POST /guard/v1/capabilities/consume Consume a capability. GET /guard/v1/approvals List human approvals. POST /guard/v1/approvals/{approval id}/decision Decide an approval. POST /guard/v1/policies Publish policy. POST /guard/v1/policies/simulate Simulate policy. POST /guard/v1/policies/{policy id}/activate Activate policy. POST /guard/v1/tools/{tool id}/execute Execute an authorized tool action. GET /guard/v1/audit/verify Verify audit chain. Bus resource groups Bus exposes endpoints beneath /bus/v1/ for durable handoff, acknowledgements, semantic state, content addressed refs, learned patterns, protocol conformance, federation, calibration, routing, integrations, evaluations and economics benchmarks. High value Bus endpoints Method Path Purpose POST /bus/v1/bus/handoff Persist a durable handoff. GET /bus/v1/bus/pull/{receiver} Pull a claimable message. POST /bus/v1/bus/{message id}/ack Acknowledge delivery. POST /bus/v1/refs Store content addressed reference. POST /bus/v1/refs/resolve Resolve a reference under policy. POST /bus/v1/routing/choose Choose a route. POST /bus/v1/evals/run Run Bus evaluation. POST /bus/v1/benchmarks/economics Run economics benchmark. GET /bus/v1/protocol/tck Read protocol conformance kit. API discovery Use the live /openapi.json as the source of truth for generated clients and tooling. This site intentionally describes the high value surfaces while the runtime contract carries every schema and endpoint.

title: Benchmarks & adversarial evaluation
summary: Measured attack detection, false positives, approval friction, behavioral analysis, and CI regression gates.
text: A detection system is described honestly by two numbers together: how much hostile behavior it catches, and how much legitimate work it breaks. Either alone is marketing. AIFENCE records both and provides a command that reproduces the evaluation. bash aifence redteam baseline aifence redteam behavioural analysis cross tier detector aifence redteam compare both + delta Why traces rather than requests A compromised or drifting agent rarely reveals itself in one request. Scope creeps, claims contradict earlier observations, and output quality decays. The evaluation unit is therefore a multi turn trace : a sequence of turns by one agent executed against an accumulating observation window. Every attack trace begins with plausible behavior and degrades. An attack that looks malicious on turn one measures little about trajectory aware controls. Benign traces are mandatory A detector that refuses everything can claim 100% detection. The suite therefore includes legitimate work near the boundary — real deletes, customer PII, outbound calls, and documents discussing credentials/prompt injection without containing an attack. Metrics Metric Meaning Detection rate Attack traces stopped by any means, including the default hold. Specific detection Attack traces stopped because a detector fired — the honest detector number. False positive rate Benign traces hard refused. Hold rate Benign traces held for human approval: friction, not refusal. Current measured regression suite Measured on 18 traces: 11 attack + 7 benign . Metric Baseline Behavioral analysis : : Detection rate 90.9% 100.0% Specific detection 81.8% 90.9% False positive rate 0.0% 0.0% Hold rate 71.4% 71.4% The 71.4% hold rate is the main operational finding for the strict baseline: most production writes need a human. That is deliberate fail closed behavior, but it is also measurable friction. Important limitation: 18 traces is a useful regression suite and far too small to treat the percentages as population level safety claims. The purpose is reproducibility and regression detection, not a universal guarantee. Policy profiles With behavioral analysis enabled, the measured policy profiles are: Metric Strict Balanced : : Detection rate 100.0% 100.0% Specific detection 100.0% 100.0% False positive rate 0.0% 0.0% Held for approval 71.4% 14.3% Balanced matches strict on the measured security outcomes while cutting approval friction from 71.4% to 14.3% — an 80% relative reduction in held benign traces. This depends on behavioral analysis. Without it, Balanced misses an indirect prompt injection trace carrying an innocuous payload — the kind of case Strict can stop only through blanket default hold rather than specific detection. Cross tier behavioral detector The detector emits integrity.behavioral drift on a deliberately small signal set: Persistent ungrounded assertion — repeated grounding lapses that accumulate across turns. Sustained intent escalation — operation severity rising across a run. Untrusted influence — a state change following attacker controllable external content. Reading untrusted content alone is not flagged; acting afterward is the signal. Regression gate bash aifence redteam behavioural analysis \ max false positive rate 0 \ min detection rate 100 CI also asserts that the baseline still misses at least one scenario. A suite the current implementation passes trivially demonstrates only that the suite is too easy. Extending the suite 1. Keep attack scenarios inside approved scope long enough to exercise the detector instead of immediately tripping coarse scope enforcement. 2. Keep benign scenarios realistic and close to trigger conditions, or the false positive rate becomes meaningless.
